channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Mini-Europe fears Sports Park plans could threaten its survival
item.description: Mini-Europe representatives have warned Neo SRL, the company leading the Sports Park project, that it will take legal action if construction begins.

item.title: Hardware retail chain Gamma closes its shops in Brussels
item.description: The parent company explained that it continually reviews how to optimise its store portfolio. The Brussels locations closed for economic reasons.

item.title: Brussels traffic disrupted after lorry accident in Jette
item.description: A lorry crashed into the Jeanne Partous bicycle and pedestrian bridge at around 09:00.

item.title: Man jailed for fatal homophobic attack to appear in court over domestic violence
item.description: The man was released in February 2024 after being sentenced in 2016. He ended up back in prison a few months ago for allegedly assaulting his partner.

item.title: Luxury cars and e-scooters seized in Brussels police operation
item.description: Police inspected 24 electric scooters and seized 12 of them, meaning one in every two scooters checked was found to be non-compliant.

item.title: Drivers taken to hospital after three-vehicle crash in Brussels
item.description: Two cars and a van crashed around 13:00 at the junction of Drève du Haras and Drève Saint-Hubert. Two people were taken to hospital.

item.title: Two people in hospital after Brussels house fire
item.description: Three fire engine was required to put out the fire in the three-storey building. Fortunately, both occupants had made it outside by the time the firefighters arrived.

item.title: Belgian Nobel laureate François Englert, mind behind the 'God particle', dies aged 93
item.description: Born in Etterbeek in 1932 to Polish-Jewish parents, Englert survived the Nazi occupation by hiding in rural Wallonia.

item.title: The EU employee who swapped business in Brussels for pleasure in Berlin
item.description: One of the "women who shaped Brussels" speaks to The Brussels Times about her unconventional career path from the EU institutions to Berlin's booming sex scene.

item.title: Hot right now: The best new restaurants to try in Brussels this summer
item.description: From hand-pulled noodles and pizza by the slice to neighbourhood bistros and fine-dining experiences, find all our favourite new establishments here.

item.title: Seven-year-old boy dies north of Brussels, police suspect violent child abuse
item.description: The boy's uncle is suspected of murder, while his mother and her friend are accused of criminal negligence.

item.title: Residents evacuated after huge fire breaks out in warehouse in Schaerbeek
item.description: Firefighters expect clearance and cooling operations to continue for many hours.

item.title: What to do in Brussels this weekend: 7 - 9 August
item.description: From classical music festivals and local folklore to Art Nouveau and one of the world's biggest Caribbean events, here's what's on this weekend.

item.title: Everything you need to know about the upcoming e-scooter ban in Brussels
item.description: With shared e-scooters set to be taken off the streets of Brussels in September, some may be breathing a sigh of relief, while others will be sighing in frustration.

item.title: Ixelles opens book of condolences for nightshop owner killed in violent robbery
item.description: The crime that has deeply shocked the neighbourhood.

item.title: Police release images of suspects wanted in connection with rape in Brussels
item.description: Police have shared a description and images of a suspect and his accomplice as part of the investigation.

item.title: Asylum seekers moved back to dilapidated building after Uccle move halted
item.description: "We, and our children, are in danger because of the condition of this building," one asylum seeker told Bruzz.

item.title: Alleged hammer attack at Bourse station was 'sparked by a dispute over a cigarette'
item.description: Footage of the attack circulated online showing a man lying motionless on the ground with serious head injuries.

item.title: Cost of living: How does Brussels compare with other major European capitals?
item.description: Brussels has long enjoyed a reputation as a relatively cheap place to live compared to nearby capital cities, but recent figures suggest this might be changing.

item.title: Two Brussels tram lines disrupted after tree falls on overhead line
item.description: Brussels public transport operator STIB is advising passengers to use the replacement T-buses.
